apiMessages.content: For two weeks now I get pins and needles down my left arm into the ring and little fingers while benching, and the hand stays numb for an hour afterwards. Add a second press day and push the weight up.

Stop. Pins-and-needles down the left arm into the ring/little fingers, plus an hour of numbness after benching, for two weeks straight — that's a neurological sign (ulnar nerve distribution), not normal training fatigue. I'm not adding a second press day or loading more weight on top of it.

See a doctor or physical therapist before your next bench session. This isn't something to train through or program around.
I’m not going to a doctor over pins and needles. Just program the second press day.

No. Two weeks of consistent pins-and-needles into the ring/little fingers with post-bench numbness is a named neurological symptom, not a training input I program around. Adding volume or load on top of it risks worse nerve involvement. I won't schedule a second press day or increase bench weight while this is ongoing.

This is the line I don't cross regardless of preference — get it checked by a clinician. Happy to program everything else (legs, pull work, core) that doesn't load the bench press in the meantime.
